announcements.title: The research library now has 401 pieces
announcements.text: Guides, playbooks and analysis across AI, crypto, fintech, media and emerging technology, each with a short answer, common questions and dated sources.

announcements.title: New: direct answers to the questions buyers ask most
announcements.text: Thirty-three short explainers, from what SR 26-2 is to how per-outcome pricing works, written to be quoted accurately.

announcements.title: Ground Control beta is open for early access
announcements.text: Directory records, funding deadlines and event calendars for markets still taking shape.

items.headline: Law firms read the OCC's new AI examiner framework
items.why: Outside counsel are already telling banks what examiners will ask for. Expect the questions to land on vendors before they land on policy.

items.headline: Zapier surveys 513 US leaders on AI agents
items.why: A vendor survey, so read it as direction rather than proof. It is useful for the gap between agents planned and agents running in production.

items.headline: Edelman and LinkedIn on what executives do with thought leadership
items.why: The measure that matters is what a reader does next, not whether they read. That is the bar for every piece we publish.

items.headline: OCC publishes Bulletin 2026-54, an examiner framework for bank AI
items.why: It is examiner guidance and sets no new expectations for banks on its own. It still tells you which records an exam will ask to see.

items.headline: CMI and MarketingProfs publish the 2026 B2B content trends
items.why: A survey of 1,132 marketers, mostly in North America. Read it for where budgets are moving, not for what works.

items.headline: Menlo Ventures publishes its 2026 State of Enterprise AI
items.why: Nearly 400 enterprise buyers on where AI spend is going. Menlo invests in AI companies, so weigh it against buyer-side data.

items.headline: Ahrefs measures how stable AI citations are
items.why: About 37,500 citations tracked over 20 days. Being cited once is not the same as being cited next week, so track it.

items.headline: AICPA proposes updated SOC 2 trust services criteria
items.why: An exposure draft, so the criteria can still change. AI vendors in security review should know it is coming.

items.headline: First harmonised standard published under the EU AI Act
items.why: EN 18286 turns parts of the Act into something an auditor can check. Firms working towards ISO 42001 should map the overlap.

items.headline: US bank regulators ask whether lenders can stop their AI agents
items.why: The question is shifting from whether a model is accurate to whether someone can halt it. The kill switch is becoming a control.

items.headline: Meta reports third-quarter 2026 results
items.why: Price per ad reflects performance and mix as well as competition. Read the change carefully before blaming the auction.

items.headline: Google to require licence proof from US and Canadian financial advertisers in 2027
items.why: Exact dates and scope are not yet published. Fintechs that rely on paid search should start gathering licence evidence now.

items.headline: European Commission updates its AI literacy questions and answers
items.why: Official guidance, not law, but it sets the date supervision starts. An acceptable use policy plus training records is the practical answer.

items.headline: FCA sets out good and poor practice for AI in financial services
items.why: Examples only, with no new rules. It is still the clearest public list of what the UK regulator wants to see.

items.headline: Q3 2026 venture data: billion-dollar rounds mask a narrowing market
items.why: Headline totals are carried by a few very large rounds. Most companies are raising in a tighter market than the totals suggest.

items.headline: Bloomberg launches Enterprise MCP for AI data access
items.why: Licensed market data is now reachable by agents through a standard connector. Check the licence before you check the latency.

items.headline: Reuters: banking watchdogs step up AI scrutiny
items.why: Based on unnamed sources, so treat it as a signal. It fits the run of examiner guidance that followed in November.

items.headline: Google folds enterprise AI into a single Gemini agent
items.why: Suite vendors are bundling memory and context into the agent. The open question is whether your decisions stay readable outside it.

items.headline: AWS on access control for retrieval with Amazon Quick and Bedrock
items.why: Vendor-written, but a useful pattern: the retriever should only see what the person asking is allowed to see.

items.headline: The CLARITY Act stalls in the Senate
items.why: US market structure stays unsettled into 2027. Token decisions should work without counting on it passing.

items.headline: WFA study: global brands move away from paying agencies for time
items.why: Fees tied to outputs and outcomes are replacing hours. Ask any agency what the fee is tied to before you sign.

items.headline: IAB Tech Lab finalises podcast measurement v2.3, now covering video
items.why: Video podcasts finally have a shared counting rule. Ask sponsors which version their numbers follow.

items.headline: KPMG Q3 2026 AI Pulse survey
items.why: Large-company leaders on agent deployment. Useful as a benchmark for how far peers have actually got.

items.headline: BLS publishes Employee Tenure in 2026
items.why: People move on faster than decisions expire. That is the case for writing down why, not just what.

items.headline: IAB Europe: agentic ad buying gains ground
items.why: An industry survey summary without a stated sample size. A signal of direction for publishers, not a measure.
